items.label: X-Fab press release: X-FAB breaks ground on new cleanroom in Erfurt (10-05-2026)
items.signal_prefix: X-FAB broke ground on a new cleanroom at its Erfurt site (Fab4Micro project)

set.signal: X-FAB broke ground on a new cleanroom at its Erfurt site (Fab4Micro project): X-FAB MEMS Foundry GmbH is expanding its manufacturing capacity for highly integrated microsystems and photonics, continuing the transition of the Erfurt site into the group's microsystems hub and creating a foundation for industrial-scale production of highly integrated microsystems and photonics solutions. The facility is intended to support growing demand from the automotive, industrial and medical end markets; the Fab4Micro project is receiving a total of EUR 127.4 million in funding from the German federal government and the Free State of Thuringia under the EU Chips Act.
set.figure: EUR 127.4 million EU Chips Act funding (German federal government and Free State of Thuringia)

items.reason: Question 56 (2026-10-19): a public grant / subsidy for a capacity project is a company fact (capex funding), not a financing term - the amount the release states is added to the existing entry.
items.evidence: The Fab4Micro project is receiving a total of Euro 127.4 million in funding from the German federal government and the Free State of Thuringia under the EU Chips Act.

items.label: IBM Q2 FY2026 (07-22-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Arvind Krishna: 'quantum computing is no longer decades away.

set.signal: CEO Arvind Krishna: 'quantum computing is no longer decades away. It is upon us, we are investing aggressively'; with the U.S. Department of Commerce IBM announced a letter of intent to build Anderon, which IBM calls the world's first pure-play quantum foundry, supported by $1 billion in CHIPS incentives provided by the Department of Commerce and a $1 billion cash contribution by IBM, and disclosed plans to invest more than $10 billion in quantum over the next five years (R&D, CapEx, manufacturing scale-up, M&A, ecosystem expansion), supporting IBM's roadmap to installing in 2029 the world's first large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer.
set.figure: Anderon: $1 billion CHIPS incentives (Department of Commerce letter of intent) plus $1 billion IBM cash contribution; more than $10 billion quantum investment over five years; fault-tolerant quantum computer in 2029

items.reason: Question 88 (2026-10-19): government incentives / grants a company receives are company facts; the 10-18 verifier had stripped the CHIPS incentive amount from this call entry as financing.
items.evidence: a letter of intent to build Anderon, the world's first pure-play quantum foundry, supported by $1 billion in chips incentives provided by the Department of Commerce and a $1 billion-dollar cash contribution by IBM

items.label: Quantinuum Q2 FY2026 (08-11-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Raj Hazra: during the second quarter Quantinuum strengthened its supply chain

set.signal: CEO Raj Hazra: during the second quarter Quantinuum strengthened its supply chain and scaled its manufacturing ecosystem: it entered a letter of intent with the U.S. Department of Commerce's CHIPS R&D office that provides up to $100 million to Quantinuum to support advanced manufacturing for the trapped-ion modality in the United States, accelerating its strategic partnerships with GlobalFoundries (critical integrated photonics and cryogenic electronics capabilities) and Monarch Quantum (high-reliability photonic components) to build or extend its supply chain to onshore suppliers. items.label: AstraZeneca 6-K (07-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: The strategic collaboration and licence agreement with CSPC Pharmaceuticals closed on 14 April 2026

set.signal: The strategic collaboration and licence agreement with CSPC Pharmaceuticals closed on 14 April 2026; the companies will initially progress four programmes that use CSPC's AI-driven peptide drug discovery platform and its proprietary LiquidGel once-monthly dosing platform technology.
